description.narrative: Normal 0 false false false EN-US JA AR-SA /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Table Normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0cm; mso-para-margin-right:0cm; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0cm; line-height:107%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:11.0pt; font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family:Arial; mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi; mso-ansi-language:EN-US; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} table.MsoTableGrid {mso-style-name:"Table Grid\,GT0\,TabelEcorys"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-priority:59; mso-style-unhide:no; mso-style-qformat:yes; border:solid windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt:solid windowtext .5pt; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-border-insideh:.5pt solid windowtext; mso-border-insidev:.5pt solid windowtext; mso-para-margin:0cm; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:10.0pt; font-family:"Times New Roman",serif; mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman"; mso-ansi-language:EN-US; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} The project will deliver socio-economic benefits and decent rural employment by (1) increasing the productivity and sustainability of agricultural production as the main livelihood strategy of the population in targeted river basins, (2) building agricultural value chains for maximising local value addition and thus socio-economic benefits, (3) promoting gender equality in reaping benefits from agriculture and the utilisation of natural resources, (4) facilitating private investments into sustainable and regenerative rice-based food systems, and (5) increasing the resilience of social-environmental systems in targeted river basins. Contributions to FAO’s Four Pillars of Decent Work are presented in Table 2. Community level livelihood investments will be based on public-private-investment plans (Output 2.1.1) and be focused on food systems transformation for long-term sustainability. The project will support community enterprises in business upskilling and market expansion, which will contribute to local employment, especially those for women and youth, as well as indigenous people. Enhanced agricultural practices and agriculture-based value chains and enterprises will secure resilient livelihoods and employment, while contributing to cultural preservation of members of Indigenous Peoples. Furthermore, the project will take necessary action to prevent child labour (between 15-17 years will be considered as children) while the project covers youth (mainly 15-29 years old group) for project benefits. Table 2: Project contributions to socio-economic benefits and rural employment FAO Pillars of Decent Work Project contribution (including corresponding Output) Pillar 1: Employment creation & enterprise development § Local community and Indigenous People’s members (f/m) supported in accessing markets & modern value chains (3.2.2, 3.3.1, 3.3.2) § Rural communities and enterprises supported in accessing markets, training, green and responsible investment, and other productive assets (2.1.1, 2.1.2) § Employment-centred livelihoods diversification mechanisms supported (3.3.1, 3.3.2) Pillar 2: Social protection § n/a Pillar 3: Standards and rights at work § Socially responsible agricultural production supported, specifically to reduce gender and age-based discrimination (3.2.1) Pillar 4: Governance and social dialogue § Strengthening democratic organizations and networks of producers and workers (3.1.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.2) § Representation of the rural poor in social dialogue and policy dialogue through their organizations supported (1.1.2, 3.1.1) § Participation of rural poor in local decision-making and governance mechanisms supported (1.1.2, 3.1.1) § Rural women and youth groups empowered to be involved in these processes from the initial steps (1.1.2, 3.1.1) § Synergies built between organizations, programmes, countries and producer-to-producer learning opportunities created (1.1.2, 4.1.1, 4.1.2) The project will ensure that project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. This includes providing occupational safety and health training and clarifying what constitutes child labour as part of value chain training or other relevant activities
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
